text:
incident-bot: :warning: Alert — High paging + streaming stalls detected on prod-cluster-7. Metric: kv_cache_size increased 9x over 15m, paging events spiked, token cadence stalled for streaming sessions. Auto-severity: P1.
Oncall Maya: saw this, grabbing pager. confirming impact on hosted API latency and some 503s. tagging eng-runtime + eng-sre.
Evan (eng-runtime): I'm on it. Any recent deploys to runtime?
Priya (eng-sre): There's a canary of continuous-batcher v2 that rolled at 04:12 UTC (6 instances on cluster-7). It changed batch accumulation heuristics and cache pinning.
Evan (eng-runtime): that aligns. batcher v2 started keeping stronger KV references to avoid cache misses — suspect leak + cache pinning bug.
Carlos (customer-success): seeing multiple customer reports, biggest is acme-corp seeing stalled streaming responses (clients see initial chunk then long silence). They flagged for SLA impact.
Oncall Maya: are 503s from OOM or from degraded scheduler? logs?
Evan (eng-runtime): grabbing logs. here's tail from runtime-54: ```
2026-03-15T04:28:12Z WARN kv_cache::eviction unable to free pages target=0 free=0
2026-03-15T04:28:14Z ERROR streaming::cadence stall detected session=abc123 last_token_ts=162s
2026-03-15T04:28:20Z INFO batching::queue size=2048 max_expected=256
```
Priya (eng-sre): batch queue growth -> backpressure -> scheduler thrash -> streaming partial flush not triggered because KV cache locks held. So streaming stalls.
Sam (eng-platform): we can temporarily scale up cluster-7 nodes to buy time, but root cause needs revert/hotfix. scaling now?
Oncall Maya: please scale +1 GPU pool immediately. Sam?
Sam (eng-platform): scaling started, ETA 90s.
deploy-bot: Started scale operation: add_gpus job-id=op-8792 status=initiated.
Evan (eng-runtime): plan A: roll back continuous-batcher v2 to v1 on cluster-7 canaries, then monitor. Plan B if rollback slow: patch to batcher config to cap batch_queue_size and force aggressive evictions: set batcher.max_items=512 and kv_cache.eviction_threshold=0.6.
Priya (eng-sre): I can push config change faster (no binary change). Recommend config first to avoid rollback churn.
Oncall Maya: do it. Push config patch and bump eviction threshold.
Evan (eng-runtime): applying config via runtime-configs: ```yaml
clusters:
  cluster-7:
    continuous_batcher:
      max_items: 512
    kv_cache:
      eviction_threshold: 0.6
      aggressive_eviction: true
```
Evan (eng-runtime): pushed, reloaded config on runtime-54 and runtime-58.
Oncall Maya: any effects yet on cache size/queue?
Priya (eng-sre): within 60s: kv_cache_size growth slowed, paging rate down 78%, batch queue dropping toward normal.
Carlos (customer-success): acme-corp confirms streaming resumed for most sessions but one long-running session still stalled.
Evan (eng-runtime): that session probably hit partial-flush bug — when KV locks held during eviction, streaming flush path never completed. We'll trigger targeted restart for session owners. Planning rolling restart of the two affected runtime pods.
Oncall Maya: approve restart, target lowest-risk pods first.
Sam (eng-platform): restarting runtime-54 now (cordon -> drain -> restart). ETA ~45s.
Evan (eng-runtime): while restart goes, I'm prepping a hotpatch to batcher to short-circuit KV pinning for streaming sessions. quick patch: set kv_cache.pin_if_active=false (dev flag). If that works, we'll bake into v2 rollout.
Priya (eng-sre): monitoring SLI: 1m median latency, streaming token cadence, error-rate 5xx. Keeping customers posted.
deploy-bot: Restart job runtime-54 completed: status=success.
Carlos (customer-success): acme-corp reports streaming backlog cleared on restarted sessions, overall improvement. They're still asking for RCA and ETA for permanent fix.
Oncall Maya: summary so far: immediate mitigation = config cap + aggressive eviction + rolling restart. Impact: partial streaming stalls for subset of sessions, ~15% requests saw increased latency, ~3 customers reported degraded UX. No data loss.
Evan (eng-runtime): next steps: 1) merge hotpatch (kv_cache.pin_if_active=false) to canary branch and deploy to canaries; 2) roll back v2 if tests fail; 3) instrument extra metrics around kv pin counts. I'll open a PR and link it here.
Evan (eng-runtime): PR: https://gh/redwood/runtime/pull/823 (hotpatch + extra metrics)
Priya (eng-sre): I'll keep on-call for next 2 hours, watching paging and streaming cadence. Also suggest retro with eng-runtime tomorrow to discuss safer rollout gating.
Carlos (customer-success): I'll send status emails to impacted customers with ETA for permanent fix (ETA 24h) and note mitigation steps taken.
Oncall Maya: tagging postmortem: we'll create incident doc and include timeline, config diff, and customer impact. Triggering postmortem template now.
Oncall Maya: incident closed -> degraded-recovery at 04:32 UTC. Monitoring window 2h.
incident-bot: Incident P1 -> status set to "mitigated" by Oncall Maya at 04:32:10 UTC. Postmortem owner assigned: Priya (eng-sre).
Evan (eng-runtime): one more note: root cause likely interaction between stronger KV pinning in batcher v2 and longer-lived streaming sessions that maintain KV references. When the cache grows beyond safe limits we start paging which delays flush and causes partial flush bug to manifest. We'll add safety caps to v2 and more canary checks.
Priya (eng-sre): filing follow-up tickets: INC-892 add canary load test for streaming cadence; INC-893 add alarms for kv_pin_count and batch_queue_ratio; INC-894 patch partial-flush to timeout and force flush.
Oncall Maya: thanks everyone. if anything flares, reopen thread. :white_check_mark:
